tagline: A Theatrical VTT Engine tailored for Story-Driven Board Games.
designBaseline: 美式/叙事驱动桌游的戏剧化 VTT 引擎：以 Node-Graph 表达地图与位置，以通用 Entity 表达配件与角色，以 JSON 规则树驱动事件流和 CCFOLIA 风格 Cut-in 自动演出。
validationScenario: Local testing only: MVP and later E2E validation use ignored LOTR fixture at local-fixtures/lotr/LotR-FotF, including image-pack manifest, sliced cards, board assets, and LOTRRule.pdf.

features.title: Load and Save Scenario Packages
features.description: Implement the MVP .lorecanvas load/save boundary for a purely manual prototype. Import must restore the same playable state without requiring rules, Cut-in actions, online services, or LOTR-specific branches. The LOTR local fixture LotR-FotF should be usable as future validation input, but the implementation must stay generic.

features.title: Edit/Run Manual Board Prototype
features.description: Build the smallest usable Edit/Run split on top of scenario load/save. Edit mode edits the scenario definition only and exposes four editable state panels: Board State for scenario-wide/global state such as trackers, decks, event piles, setup variables, and metadata; Object State for any Entity/Object such as character pawns, troop stacks, cards, tokens, dice, and their sheet/counter state; Location State for each Location's semantic state such as name, region/area membership, recruitment availability, terrain/tile bindings, haven/stronghold flags, slots, and notes; and Edge State for graph connection semantics such as directed/undirected movement, traversal cost, labels, locks, and notes. Edit mode also manages asset manifest, Board Template, background, Locations, Edges, board zones, default placement slots, and Setup Preset entities/cards/tokens/counters. Edit mode does not create or mutate runtime scenario state. Run mode opens a finalized scenario, freezes the Board Template and Setup Preset, derives the initial runtime snapshot from that setup, and supports semantic manual board operations: move Location-bound Entities between Locations, adjust stacked troop/token/dice counters, move cards between deck/discard/hand/display zones, inspect current state, save the runtime snapshot, and reload it. This feature intentionally ignores automatic setup parsing, event triggers, path validation, Cut-in rendering, online services, and game-specific rules.

features.title: Graph Movement Validation
features.description: Implement generic graph movement validation after the manual scenario MVP is stable. Expose an engine API that determines whether a path-capable Entity can move from its current Location to a target Location using existing Edges. The first version is adjacency/connectivity only and must not introduce grid, distance, A*, or game-specific movement assumptions.

features.title: Manual Global Tracker State
features.description: Add generic Global Trackers as manually editable scenario state. Trackers represent values such as Threat, Time, Sanity, Doom, or any scenario-defined counter, and must serialize through .lorecanvas packages. This MVP-stage tracker feature should not yet drive automatic visual filters or rule triggers.

features.title: Deferred JSON Rule Trigger Engine
features.description: After the manual MVP and serialization boundary are stable, implement the generic event listener and JSON rule tree engine. It should accept triggers such as ENTITY_MOVE, ENTITY_STATE_CHANGE, TRACKER_CHANGE, and MANUAL_TRIGGER, evaluate conditions, and emit actions without hard-coding LOTR or any other specific game.

features.title: Deferred Cut-in Renderer
features.description: Implement the CCFOLIA-style theatrical rendering lane after the rule engine exists. Cut-in payloads should support overlays, image references, slide-in presentation, typewriter text, and rule hint panels. The renderer consumes commands only and must not decide game rules.

features.title: LOTR FotF Local Validation Fixture
features.description: Use the ignored local fixture local-fixtures/lotr/LotR-FotF for end-to-end validation. The fixture includes renamed component image assets, sliced cards, dice faces, the complete game board artwork, and LOTRRule.pdf as a simplified player rule summary for future auto-setup and event-trigger tests. Initial validation should prove that a generic .lorecanvas package can import the asset pack, restore an Edit-mode Board Template with Locations, Edges, regions/areas, zones, default placement slots, and a Setup Preset, then open it in Run mode as a frozen runtime board and round-trip runtime changes through save/load. Later validation may add auto-setup, movement, tracker, rule-trigger, and Cut-in coverage without polluting the generic engine with LOTR-specific branches.

mvpFocus.summary: After F-03 scenario load/save, prioritize a split between Edit mode and Run mode. Edit mode defines Board Template and Setup Preset. Run mode freezes those definitions, derives runtime state, and supports manual semantic board operations before movement validation, rule triggers, global visual automation, or Cut-in rendering.

modeModel.editMode: Edits setup definition only through four state surfaces plus structural assets: Board State for global scenario state, Object State for Entity/Object state, Location State for per-Location semantic state, and Edge State for per-connection semantic state. It also edits asset manifest, Board Template, background, Locations, Edges, zones, default placement slots, and Setup Preset entities/cards/tokens/counters. It does not create runtime scenario state.
modeModel.runMode: Consumes a finalized scenario definition, freezes Board Template and Setup Preset, derives an initial runtime snapshot, then allows manual runtime operations such as moving Location-bound Entities, adjusting stacks/counters, moving cards between zones, and saving/reloading current runtime state.

fixtureNotes: local-fixtures/lotr/LotR-FotF is ignored local validation data, not product assets.
LOTRRule.pdf is a player-written simplified rule summary reserved for future auto-setup and event-trigger tests.
Load/save must remain generic and must not hard-code LOTR semantics.
